verdict: Acceptable with small polish. The current HSConfig static-semantics model is broad enough for no-block pre-run Wild packages and the 11-plus-1 proof set stays lean, but current 2026 mechanics such as Rewind, Herald, and Shatter still rely on unknown-warning drift visibility instead of explicit support rows, and the deck set still under-exercises secret, freeze, location, discover-control, and questline-heavy families.

deck_matrix_observations: The live proof set is still 12 decks total: 11 representative rows in `docs/operator/archetype-fixture-matrix.json` plus supplemental `CuteWarrior` in `docs/operator/supplemental-proof-decks.json`.

The representative matrix covers the main shell families HSConfig already handles well for no-block preparation: ShadowPriest covers aggro burn and hero-power transform, CtAPaladin and BigShaman cover recruit, BigShaman adds big-minion and deathrattle cheat, Discolock covers discard, TreantDruid covers token or aura snowball, ImbueMage covers hero-power plus generated-entity adjacency, MechPala covers mech scaling, Kingslayer and PirateRogue cover weapon pressure, Boarlock covers combo-control with `Combo.json`, and PirateDH adds pirate hero-attack pressure.

CuteWarrior adds the low-curve Warrior shell without widening the representative matrix. The supplemental deck remains correctly marked as `supplemental_load_safe_only`, not representative output competence, and does not close Kingslayer or Boarlock source-depth gaps.

The current deck set exercises several important direct or partial lanes in practice: weapon, recruit, discard, generated-entity adjacency, imbue, hero-power transform, combo-control, pirate pressure, mech scaling, and big-minion cheat.

The current deck set does not directly exercise dedicated discover, choose-one, secret, freeze, location, overload-first, questline, board-position, generic-spell-target, Rewind, Herald, or Shatter families through a named representative row. Those support claims currently come more from the code registry and no-block contract than from deck-matrix proof.

That split is acceptable for a lean no-block repo. It is not enough to claim that every modern Wild mechanic is already first-class deck-proven, but it is enough to claim that the package generator is broad across major Wild shell families without over-expanding the repository.
no_block_assessment: The no-block promise should stay tied to `technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE`, `runtime_load_safe=true`, `runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply`, and the required minimal runtime files, not to first-class support for every modern keyword.

Identity-gated direct is the correct boundary for `choose_one`, `discover`, and `hero_power_transform`: HSConfig should only lower those surfaces directly when the exact option or transformed identity is source-backed.

Partial mechanics such as `generated_entity`, `freeze`, `destroy`, `silence`, `transform`, `secret`, `location`, `questline`, `imbue`, and `spellburst` should keep lowering only the parts that map cleanly to documented VisionAI surfaces while the signature unresolved action remains report-only when needed.

Registered warning-only mechanics such as `kindred`, `tourist`, `starship`, `tradeable`, `dredge`, `forge`, `titan`, `secret_timing`, `location_activation`, `board_position`, and `generic_spell_target` are correctly descriptive and must not block load-safe apply.

Current but unmapped mechanics such as `rewind`, `herald`, and `shatter` should be treated as unknown-warning mechanics today: visible in drift reporting, non-blocking for valid packages, and not lowered into invented runtime rows until an exact documented surface exists.
skill_slimness_assessment: The current design remains slim because it prefers explicit warning boundaries and mechanic drift reporting over widening the representative matrix or inventing runtime behavior for unsupported mechanics.
Keeping `CuteWarrior` supplemental preserves the useful governance split: 11 representative decks for durable proof plus 1 narrow low-curve Warrior acceptance deck for extra shell coverage.

Adding explicit no-block registry or drift entries for `rewind`, `herald`, and `shatter` would stay within the lean HSConfig boundary because it expands visibility, not post-run tuning scope, runtime writes, or HSTuner behavior.

The main anti-pattern to avoid is compensating for every new mechanic with another full representative deck. For this skill, mechanic visibility tables and one-at-a-time targeted additions are cheaper and clearer than open-ended matrix growth.
gaps_or_risks: The live collectible-card probe on 2026-07-10 found current mechanics that are active in Hearthstone but not explicitly registered in HSConfig today, especially `rewind`, `herald`, and `shatter`. Those currently rely on unknown-warning drift behavior rather than named support rows.

The representative deck matrix does not currently prove dedicated discover, choose-one, secret, freeze, location, overload-first, or questline-heavy control shells, so some identity-gated-direct and partial categories are supported more by code policy than by deck-fixture evidence.

Registered warning-only support for `kindred`, `tourist`, and `starship` is honest and safe, but it also means decks centered on those mechanics only get descriptive pre-run semantics instead of first-class action lowering.

Current Wild shell diversity can shift quickly with balance patches and new sets, so the matrix is representative rather than exhaustive. That is fine for a no-block generator, but it is not proof of universal mechanic completeness.
Promoting `CuteWarrior` into the representative matrix now would add size without adding a clearly missing family, so it would increase maintenance cost more than semantic confidence.
recommended_next_action: Add explicit non-blocking registry or drift-detection entries for `rewind`, `herald`, and `shatter`, defaulting them to warning-only unless a documented VisionAI lowering surface already exists.
confidence: high - the verdict is consistent across the live HSConfig registry, same-day collectible-card keyword probe, official Blizzard mechanic announcements, and targeted local verification with 32 passing tests on 2026-07-10
